name: Principal Financial Group, Inc.
moat_justification: Moderate/narrow finance moat: a sticky, scaled U.S. retirement franchise for small and mid-sized employers (defined contribution, defined benefit, pension risk transfer and ESOP services, bundled with group benefits and protection) plus a diversified global asset-management arm — workplace distribution and long-duration plan relationships are hard to replicate quickly and OE was positive in 5 of the last 5 fiscal years — against commodity, price-competed products with no structural pricing power: asset-management fees face passive/fee compression and active-equity outflows from much larger rivals (Vanguard, Fidelity, BlackRock), spread and premium earnings are hostage to rates, credit and markets rather than Principal's own pricing, legacy exited annuity/life blocks still inject reinsurance embedded-derivative volatility into GAAP results, and insurance regulation/capital intensity caps returns.
fragility_flags: STALE_FY: latest fiscal year ended 9 months ago — check TTM/quarterly OE and consider --base-oe-ps override
BUYBACK_TAILWIND: share count shrinking 4.0%/yr — already credited via the growth adjustment
NI_OCF_DIVERGENCE: net income and operating cash flow differ by >40% in 2023, 2024, 2025 — find the one-off (tax deposits, impairments, WC swings) before trusting the OE base
SECTOR_MODEL_MISMATCH: Finance sector — OE/capex DCF fits finance names poorly; grade confidence low

OVERRIDE_APPLIED:capex — filing gap in the last 3 FY filled by a judgment override (filing: Form 10-K for fiscal year ended December 31, 2025 (filed 2026-02-18), Consolidated Statements of Cash Flows, investing activities line 'Net purchases of property and equipment': $(98.0) million for FY2025, with $(68.8) million for FY2024 and $(102.0) million for FY2023 in the same statement (all in $ millions)); an override never replaces a filed value — see overrides_applied and override_impact
WIDE_SCENARIO_SPREAD: super-bull IV is 4.5x super-bear IV — uncertainty is huge; confidence should not be high
one_liner: Diversified retirement/benefits/asset-management insurer, moat 5/10 — engine prints Tier A (weighted IRR 21.71%, IV@15% $167.94 vs $107.81) on an OCF base that capitalizes insurer float, so the final tier is softened to B at low confidence; it clears 15% at ~$168 on engine numbers, with a materially lower true margin of safety.
tier_override_reason: SECTOR_MODEL_MISMATCH insurer artifact: the OCF-based OE base capitalizes float/reserve growth (NI_OCF_DIVERGENCE is structural in 2023, 2024 and 2025 — FY2025 OCF $4,536,700,000 vs net income $1,185,100,000, and maintenance OE $1,338,500,000 vs conservative OE $4,328,800,000), so tier-by-numbers A overstates distributable owner's earnings; softened one notch to B, confidence low — same treatment as HIG/ACGL/WRB.
moat_for: Sticky SMB retirement franchise — leading defined-contribution, pension risk transfer and ESOP provider; workplace plan relationships are long-duration and bundled with other products
Diversified earnings mix — retirement fees, benefits & protection premiums, asset-management fees and spread income dampen any single product cycle
Scale and distribution — established advisor/employer channels for mid-market employers that larger, scale-focused rivals underserve
Through-cycle profitability and capital return — OE positive 5 of last 5 FY; diluted shares shrinking 4.0%/yr on buybacks
moat_against: No structural pricing power — retirement, benefits and asset-management products are price-competed; fees face passive compression and active-equity outflows
Market and rate hostage — AUM fees, net investment income and spreads ride equity markets and the yield curve, outside management control
Legacy exited-block volatility — funds-withheld reinsurance embedded derivative swung to a large loss in Q2 2026 and drove the exited-business pre-tax loss well above the prior year
Capital intensity and regulation — insurance capital rules cap growth and capital return; larger rivals carry bigger technology/compliance budgets

overrides.source: Form 10-K for fiscal year ended December 31, 2025 (filed 2026-02-18), Consolidated Statements of Cash Flows, investing activities line 'Net purchases of property and equipment': $(98.0) million for FY2025, with $(68.8) million for FY2024 and $(102.0) million for FY2023 in the same statement (all in $ millions)
